home.heroText: Psychological rock and roll built on two bass guitars, drums and one unmistakable voice.
home.introText: BEAST came out of Cape Town in 2012 with a deliberately unusual setup: two bass guitars, drums and Inge Beckmann's voice. Heavy, raw and stripped of the usual lead-guitar architecture.

members.name: Inge Beckmann
members.bio: Frontwoman of Cape Town art-rock outfit Lark before its semi-permanent hiatus. Joined BEAST once the two-bass experiment 'sounded right', bringing a method-singing approach that swings between a whisper and a howl. She pushed for a name with an 'interesting visual effect' — Bow Beast — before the band settled on BEAST.

members.name: Rian Zietsman
members.bio: Guitarist of Taxi Violence who bought a bass with Louis Nel in late 2011 purely to learn the instrument. Plays the low, rhythmic end of the twin-bass setup, holding the floor while the second bass climbs over it.

members.name: Louis Nel
members.bio: Taxi Violence's drummer, turned bassist. Runs a higher, chord-based lead approach through a guitar amp — the reason BEAST sounds rawer and more low-fi than a standard rock four-piece.

members.name: Werner von Waltsleben
members.bio: Drummer of Afrikaans metal band Kobus!. A long-time fan of both Taxi Violence and Lark, he called joining BEAST 'a dream come true' — a chance to play the music he wanted to hear.

pastMember.name: Sasha Righini
pastMember.bio: Drummer of The Plastics, invited into the basement sessions early and soon a full member. Left in mid-2013 to pursue his own music.

band.instrumentation: The twin-bass setup is rare in South African music. Zietsman plays low and rhythmic like a normal bassist; Nel plays higher and chord-based like a lead guitarist, through a guitar amp. The result is rawer, harder and more low-fi than a standard four-piece.

timeline.title: The two-bass experiment begins
timeline.copy: Rian Zietsman and Louis Nel buy bass guitars and begin jamming in the basement of the house they share. Sasha Righini joins on drums and the project develops from an experiment into a band.

timeline.title: Kombass becomes BEAST
timeline.copy: The early working name Kombass gives way to BEAST after Inge Beckmann joins on vocals. The stripped setup is fixed: two bass guitars, drums and voice.

timeline.title: First Cape Town shows
timeline.copy: By May 2012 BEAST are being billed at The Assembly in Cape Town as a new supergroup featuring members of Lark, Taxi Violence and The Plastics.

timeline.title: Oppikoppi Sweet Thing
timeline.copy: BEAST join the 9–11 August Oppikoppi bill in Northam. Contemporary festival coverage later lists the band among the weekend highlights.

timeline.title: Smoke Swig Swear recorded
timeline.copy: The debut album is recorded over four days in September at Sound and Motion Studios in Cape Town, keeping the twin-bass sound raw and direct.

timeline.title: Rocking the Daisies
timeline.copy: BEAST play the sold-out Rocking the Daisies festival at Cloof Wine Estate in Darling during the 4–7 October weekend.

timeline.title: Synergy Live
timeline.copy: On 30 November BEAST play the main stage at Synergy Live at Theewaterskloof, scheduled 21:00–21:45 immediately before The Narrow and headliner The Prodigy.

timeline.title: Up the Creek
timeline.copy: On 1 February BEAST appear on Up the Creek's Friday-night Tribute to Women main-stage programme alongside SAARKIE, Tailor, Machineri and Karen Zoid.

timeline.title: Smoke Swig Swear launches
timeline.copy: The debut gets its official album launch at The Assembly in Cape Town on 23 February.

timeline.title: Design Indaba Music Circuit
timeline.copy: Four days after the album launch, BEAST play the Design Indaba Music Circuit at Aces n Spades as part of a three-day Cape Town programme spanning 32 artists and eight venues.

timeline.title: RAMfest
timeline.copy: BEAST are billed for RAMfest Cape Town, 7–10 March at Circle of Dreams near Riviersonderend, on a bill with Rise Against, Bring Me The Horizon and Pendulum.

timeline.title: The documentary and international press
timeline.copy: A short documentary follows the album launch, and on 28 August VICE/Noisey premieres the Smoke Swig Swear video alongside an interview with Inge Beckmann and the band's story.

timeline.title: Line-up change
timeline.copy: Sasha Righini leaves to pursue his own music and Werner von Waltsleben of Kobus! takes over on drums.

timeline.title: Crowdfunding Bardo
timeline.copy: On 13 August BEAST launch an Indiegogo campaign to fund album two while remaining unsigned and protecting their creative independence. A private investor later helps complete the record.

timeline.title: Private Bardo acoustic launch
timeline.copy: On 21 February, backers, family and friends attend an intimate acoustic launch at the Cape Town Club, with the material rearranged for a quieter setting.

timeline.title: Bardo launches publicly
timeline.copy: The second album receives its public launch on 27 February. Contemporary listings describe the record as the result of the band's 2014 fan-funded recording push.

timeline.title: Splashy Fen
timeline.copy: BEAST are announced for Splashy Fen's 2–6 April Easter-weekend edition near Underberg, joining a broad South African bill including Taxi Violence, Shortstraw, aKING and Nakhane Toure.

timeline.title: Critical peak for Bardo
timeline.copy: On 9 April the Mail & Guardian asks whether BEAST might be South Africa's finest live rock act, praising the force of the two-bass setup and Inge Beckmann's vocal range.
